22 A uniform wire is made of a metal that has a Young modulus of 1.3  1011
Pa.
The wire is 2.4 m long and has a spring constant of 2.7  104
N m–1.
What is the volume of the wire?
A
2.6  10–8
m3
B
6.3  10–8
m3
C
5.0  10–7
m3
D
1.2  10–6
m3

hints: Notice you are given stiffness as spring constant $k = 2.7 \times 10^4 \text{ N m}^{-1}$, not force and extension separately, plus $L = 2.4 \text{ m}$ and $E = 1.3 \times 10^{11} \text{ Pa}$.
Connect $E$ to $k$ using $E = (F/A)/(x/L) = kL/A$, so the unknown cross-sectional area is $A = kL/E$.
Form the cylinder volume as $V = AL = kL^2/E$ and substitute the three values, checking that $\text{N m}^{-1} \times \text{m}^2 / \text{Pa}$ gives $\text{m}^3$.
walkthrough: Identify the wire as a uniform cylinder of length $L = 2.4 \text{ m}$ and unknown area $A$, so its volume is $V = AL$.
Use spring constant $k = F/x = 2.7 \times 10^4 \text{ N m}^{-1}$ to replace $F/x$, giving $E = kL/A$.
Multiply by length for volume: $V = AL = kL^2/E = 5.0 \times 10^{-7} \times 2.4 \approx 1.2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3$.

A.explanation: Too small by about a factor of 50. It results from an error in combining $k$, $L$ and $E$, for example dividing by $L$ instead of multiplying by $L^2$.

B.explanation: Too small. It is close to $A \times L$ with $L = 2.4 \text{ m}$, so it comes from using the wrong power of length when forming the volume.

C.explanation: Too small by more than a factor of 2. It can arise from using $V = kL/E$ instead of $V = kL^2/E$ and so missing one factor of the $2.4 \text{ m}$ length.

D.explanation: Correct from $V = AL$ with $A = kL/E$, giving $V = kL^2/E \approx 1.2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3$.
